title: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

hook.en: Three questions to ask the nervous system — and how to read the answers like a map.
hook.ur: Nervous system se poochne ke teen sawal — aur un ke jawab ko naqshe ki tarah parhna.

goal.en: By the end, you'll run a quick upper- and lower-limb neuro screen and know which nerve root each finding points to.
goal.ur: End tak aap upper aur lower limb ka tez neuro screen kar sakenge aur jaan jayenge ke har finding kis nerve root ki taraf ishara karti hai.

text.en: A patient says, "The pain goes down my leg." Now you ask the nervous system three questions: Can they **FEEL** normally? Can they **PUSH** normally? Do the **REFLEXES** fire normally? Together, that's the neuro screen.
text.ur: Patient kehta hai, "Dard meri leg mein neeche jata hai." Ab aap nervous system se teen sawal poochte hain: Kya woh normal **MEHSOOS** kar sakta hai? Kya woh normal **ZOR** laga sakta hai? Kya **REFLEXES** normal hain? In teenon ko mila kar neuro screen kehte hain.

text.en:
**Dermatome**: the skin area supplied mainly by one spinal nerve root (tests sensation).
**Myotome**: the group of muscles supplied mainly by one nerve root (tests strength).
**Reflex**: an automatic muscle response that tests one root's loop into and out of the spinal cord.
text.ur:
**Dermatome**: skin ka woh hissa jise zyada tar ek spinal nerve root supply karti hai (sensation test).
**Myotome**: muscles ka woh group jise zyada tar ek nerve root supply karti hai (strength test).
**Reflex**: ek automatic muscle response jo ek root ke spinal cord mein aane jaane wale loop ko test karta hai.

simpler.en: Dermatome = skin map. Myotome = muscle map. Reflex = the automatic loop test.
simpler.ur: Dermatome = skin ka naqsha. Myotome = muscles ka naqsha. Reflex = automatic loop ka test.

text.en: Think of the spinal cord as a building with many floors. Each floor sends out its own electric line: one wire to a patch of skin, one to a set of muscles, and a loop you can test with a tap. Damage one floor's line and you find a **matching pattern**: that skin feels different, those muscles are weak, that reflex is reduced.
text.ur: Spinal cord ko kai manzilon wali imarat samjhein. Har manzil apni bijli ki line bahar bhejti hai: ek taar skin ke ek hisse tak, ek muscles ke group tak, aur ek loop jise tap kar ke test kar sakte hain. Ek manzil ki line kharab ho to **milta julta pattern** milta hai: wahi skin alag mehsoos hoti hai, wahi muscles weak, wahi reflex kam.

text.en: The reflex rhyme: **S1–2, buckle my shoe** (ankle jerk) · **L3–4, kick the door** (knee jerk) · **C5–6, pick up sticks** (biceps) · **C7–8, lay them straight** (triceps).
text.ur: Reflex ki nazm: **S1–2, buckle my shoe** (ankle jerk) · **L3–4, kick the door** (knee jerk) · **C5–6, pick up sticks** (biceps) · **C7–8, lay them straight** (triceps). English mein hi yaad rakhein — viva mein yehi kaam aati hai!

question.en: Weak big-toe extension and reduced sensation over the top of the foot. Which root is most likely involved?
question.ur: Big toe ki extension weak aur foot ki upar wali surface par sensation kam. Kaun si root zyada mumkin hai?

text.en: L4

feedback.en: L4 is tested with ankle dorsiflexion and medial-leg sensation. Big-toe extension + top of the foot point to the next level down.
feedback.ur: L4 ankle dorsiflexion aur leg ke andar wale hisse ki sensation se test hoti hai. Big toe + foot ki upar wali surface agle level ki taraf ishara karte hain.

text.en: L5

feedback.en: Yes! Great-toe extension (myotome) and dorsum of the foot (dermatome) both point to L5 — a matching pattern.
feedback.ur: Haan! Big toe ki extension (myotome) aur foot ki upar wali surface (dermatome) dono L5 ki taraf — milta julta pattern.

text.en: S1

feedback.en: S1 shows up as weak plantarflexion, lateral-foot sensation change and a reduced ankle jerk.
feedback.ur: S1 mein plantarflexion weak, foot ke bahar wale hisse ki sensation mein tabdeeli aur ankle jerk kam hota hai.

question.en: A reduced ankle jerk and numbness along the outer border of the foot. Which root?
question.ur: Ankle jerk kam aur foot ke bahar wale kinare par numbness. Kaun si root?

text.en: L3

feedback.en: L3 links to the knee (knee jerk, medial knee sensation), not the ankle jerk.
feedback.ur: L3 knee se juri hai (knee jerk, knee ke andar ki sensation), ankle jerk se nahi.

text.en: L5

feedback.en: L5 has no reliable routine reflex and supplies the top of the foot, not the outer border.
feedback.ur: L5 ka koi reliable routine reflex nahi aur woh foot ki upar wali surface supply karti hai, bahar wala kinara nahi.

text.en: S1

feedback.en: Correct — "S1–2, buckle my shoe". Ankle jerk + lateral foot = S1.
feedback.ur: Sahi — "S1–2, buckle my shoe". Ankle jerk + foot ka bahar wala hissa = S1.

prompt.en: Quick sort: is each test checking a MYOTOME or a DERMATOME?
prompt.ur: Jaldi sort karein: har test MYOTOME check kar raha hai ya DERMATOME?

text.en: Resisted shoulder abduction

why.en: Strength of a muscle group → C5 myotome.
why.ur: Muscle group ki taqat → C5 myotome.

text.en: Light touch on the thumb
Repeated heel raises
Pin-prick on the little finger
Resisted great-toe extension
Light touch at the medial malleolus

Doing it fast and well: **always compare left with right** at each level. Light touch (and pin-prick if needed) at each dermatome's key point; a resisted isometric hold for each myotome ("hold — don't let me move you"); reflexes with the patient relaxed — if a reflex seems absent, use reinforcement (the Jendrassik manoeuvre: patient pulls their hooked fingers apart) before calling it absent.
text.ur: Tez aur sahi tareeqa: har level par **hamesha left aur right ka muqabla karein**. Har dermatome ke key point par halka touch (aur zaroorat ho to pin-prick); har myotome ke liye resisted isometric hold ("rokein — mujhe hilane na dein"); reflexes patient ke relax hone par — agar reflex ghayab lage to absent kehne se pehle reinforcement karein (Jendrassik manoeuvre: patient apni interlocked fingers zor se kheenche).

text.en: Common mistakes: (1) Testing one side only. (2) Treating dermatome maps as exact borders — they overlap and vary between people, so look for a **pattern**, not a single spot. (3) Forgetting that one weak muscle can be a **peripheral nerve** problem, not a root — e.g. foot drop from a common fibular nerve injury vs an L5 radiculopathy (check hip abduction and inversion: often spared in fibular nerve palsy, weak in L5).
text.ur: Aam ghaltiyan: (1) Sirf ek side test karna. (2) Dermatome maps ko bilkul pakki sarhadein samajhna — yeh overlap karte hain aur har insaan mein thora farq hota hai, is liye ek jagah nahi, **pattern** dekhein. (3) Bhool jana ke ek weak muscle **peripheral nerve** ka masla bhi ho sakta hai, root ka nahi — maslan common fibular nerve injury se foot drop vs L5 radiculopathy (hip abduction aur inversion check karein: fibular nerve palsy mein aksar theek, L5 mein weak).

text.en: Stop and refer **the same day** if you find: saddle numbness, new bladder or bowel changes, or symptoms in **both** legs — possible cauda equina syndrome. Rapidly worsening weakness also needs urgent medical review. These are emergencies, not physiotherapy cases.
text.ur: Agar yeh milein to **usi din** ruk kar refer karein: saddle area mein numbness, bladder ya bowel mein nayi tabdeeli, ya **dono** legs mein symptoms — cauda equina syndrome ka imkaan. Tezi se barhti weakness ke liye bhi urgent medical review zaroori hai. Yeh emergencies hain, physiotherapy cases nahi.

question.en: Which finding needs URGENT referral rather than routine physiotherapy?
question.ur: Kaun si finding routine physiotherapy ke bajaye URGENT referral mangti hai?

text.en: Mildly reduced sensation on one foot after lifting, stable for a week
text.ur: Weight uthane ke baad ek foot par halki kam sensation, ek hafte se stable

feedback.en: Worth monitoring and documenting — and refer if it worsens — but on its own it's usually managed conservatively.
feedback.ur: Monitor aur document karna zaroori hai — aur barhe to refer karein — lekin akela yeh aam tor par conservative tareeqe se manage hota hai.

text.en: Saddle numbness with new difficulty passing urine
text.ur: Saddle area mein numbness aur urine pass karne mein nayi mushkil

feedback.en: Exactly — possible cauda equina syndrome. Same-day emergency referral.
feedback.ur: Bilkul — cauda equina syndrome ka imkaan. Usi din emergency referral.

text.en: Unilateral calf ache with a completely normal neuro screen
text.ur: Ek taraf calf mein dard aur neuro screen bilkul normal

feedback.en: The neuro screen is reassuring here (though always consider other causes, like a DVT, if the calf is swollen and tender).
feedback.ur: Yahan neuro screen tasalli-bakhsh hai (lekin agar calf suja hua aur tender ho to DVT jaisi doosri wajah bhi zaroor sochein).

question.en: Why test reflexes at all, if you've already tested strength and sensation?
question.ur: Agar strength aur sensation test kar li to reflexes kyun test karein?

answer.en: Reflexes depend far less on the patient's effort or interpretation, so they add an objective piece. A reduced reflex supports a lower motor neuron / root problem at that level; brisk reflexes point instead to an upper motor neuron problem (remember UMN = UP).
answer.ur: Reflexes patient ki koshish ya samajh par bohat kam depend karte hain, is liye yeh objective saboot dete hain. Kam reflex us level par lower motor neuron / root ke masle ki himayat karta hai; tez reflexes upper motor neuron ke masle ki taraf ishara karte hain (yaad rakhein UMN = UP).

summary.en: Dermatome = sensation, myotome = strength, reflex = automatic loop — look for a matching pattern.
summary.ur: Dermatome = sensation, myotome = taqat, reflex = automatic loop — milta julta pattern dhoondein.

summary.en: Know the key levels: L2–S1 and C5–T1, plus the reflex rhyme.
summary.ur: Key levels yaad rakhein: L2–S1 aur C5–T1, saath reflex ki nazm.

summary.en: Always compare sides; saddle numbness or bladder/bowel change = same-day emergency.
summary.ur: Hamesha dono sides compare karein; saddle numbness ya bladder/bowel tabdeeli = usi din emergency.

back.ur: Ankle dorsiflexion · leg ka andar wala hissa/medial malleolus · knee jerk (zyada L4).

back.en: Great-toe extension · dorsum of the foot (no reliable routine reflex).
back.ur: Big toe ki extension · foot ki upar wali surface (reliable routine reflex nahi).

back.en: Plantarflexion/eversion · lateral foot & heel · ankle jerk.
back.ur: Plantarflexion/eversion · foot aur heel ka bahar wala hissa · ankle jerk.

back.en: Elbow flexion & wrist extension · lateral forearm & thumb · brachioradialis (and biceps C5–6).
back.ur: Elbow flexion aur wrist extension · forearm ka bahar wala hissa aur thumb · brachioradialis (aur biceps C5–6).

back.en: Elbow extension & wrist flexion · middle finger · triceps jerk.
back.ur: Elbow extension aur wrist flexion · middle finger · triceps jerk.

front.en: What is the Jendrassik manoeuvre for?

back.en: Reinforcement to bring out a lower-limb reflex that seems absent (patient pulls hooked fingers apart).
back.ur: Ghayab lagte lower-limb reflex ko ubharne ke liye reinforcement (patient interlocked fingers zor se kheenchta hai).
